Replace a step

Source: R/pipeflow.R
pip_replace.Rd

Replaces a step's function while keeping it in the same position in the pipeline. Downstream steps that have run before are automatically marked as outdated and will re-run on the next pip_run().

Usage

pip_replace(x, step, fun, tags = NULL, params = list(), exec = NULL)

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pipeline or view object.

step

Unique step name.

fun

Function to execute for the step. Each function parameter needs a value: a default value in fun or an entry in params. Default values that are simple constants are resolved immediately. Default values that are formulas like ~other_step are treated as dependencies to those steps and resolved to the respective output values at runtime once the step is executed. A reference wrapped in try(), like ~try(other_step), accepts a failed input when the pipeline is run with on_error = "continue": instead of the output of the referenced step, the argument then receives a condition of class pipeflow_failure (see section 'Continuing after errors' in pip_run()). The function can refer to the running pipeline as .self (see section 'The pipeline as .self' in pip_add()).

tags

Optional character vector of tags belonging to the step. If NULL (the default), the current tags of the step are kept. Use character(0) to remove all tags.

params

Optional named list of parameter values. They override the defaults of fun and give a value to parameters of fun that have no default. As in the defaults of fun, a formula like ~other_step refers to the output of another step. Names that are no parameters of fun add params to the step, which are passed on to fun as well, so fun needs a ... argument for them. Use cases for params are:

  1. Set param values programmatically, e.g. when adding steps in a loop or at runtime.

  2. Use existing functions whose parameters have no defaults, e.g. pip_add(p, "avg", mean, params = list(x = ~data, na.rm = TRUE)).

  3. Provide extra param values to "mark" dependencies that are defined in pipelines nested in a step, which ensures that it is re-executed when one of the nested param values change. See the nested pipelines vignette.

exec

Execution mode for the step, see pip_add(). If NULL (the default), the current execution mode of the step is kept.

Value

The updated pipeline, invisibly.

Details

By default, the step keeps its tags and execution mode: tags = NULL and exec = NULL mean "keep the current value". To change them, pass explicit values, where tags = character(0) removes all tags and exec = "auto" resets the execution mode to its default. Parameters, output, state and lock status are always reset, like for a freshly added step.

Examples

p <- pip_new() |>
    pip_add("load", \(n = 5) seq_len(n)) |>
    pip_add("double", \(x = ~load) x * 2)
pip_run(p)
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.295 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'pipe'
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.295 UTC]: Step 1/2 load
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.296 UTC]: Step 2/2 double
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.297 UTC]: Finished in 0.002 s (2 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>      step params depends state            out
#> 1:   load      n          done      1,2,3,4,5
#> 2: double      x    load  done  2, 4, 6, 8,10
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-26 16:24:37 (0.002 s)
#> steps: 2 done

# Replace "load" — downstream steps are automatically marked "outdated"
pip_replace(p, "load", \(n = 3) seq_len(n))
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>      step params depends    state            out
#> 1:   load      n              new         [NULL]
#> 2: double      x    load outdated  2, 4, 6, 8,10
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-26 16:24:37 (0.002 s)
#> steps: 1 outdated, 1 new

# Re-run to bring everything up to date
pip_run(p)
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.303 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'pipe'
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.303 UTC]: Step 1/2 load
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.303 UTC]: Step 2/2 double
#> info [2026-10-26 16:24:37.304 UTC]: Finished in 0.001 s (2 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
p
#> <pipeflow> pipe (2 steps)
#> -------------------------
#>      step params depends state   out
#> 1:   load      n          done 1,2,3
#> 2: double      x    load  done 2,4,6
#> -------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-26 16:24:37 (0.001 s)
#> steps: 2 done

# If a view is passed, the step must be part of the view
v <- pip_view(p, step = "double")
pip_replace(v, "double", \(x = ~load) x * 3)
p[["state"]]                                # "double" is "new" again
#>   load double 
#> "done"  "new" 

try(pip_replace(v, "load", \(n = 2) seq_len(n)))
#> Error in pip_replace(v, "load", function(n = 2) seq_len(n)) : 
#>   step 'load' is not part of the view

# Tags and execution mode are kept unless set explicitly
pip_tag(p, "io")
pip_replace(p, "load", \(n = 4) seq_len(n))
p[, "tags"]
#>      tags
#>    <list>
#> 1:     io
#> 2:     io
pip_replace(p, "load", \(n = 4) seq_len(n), tags = character(0))
p[, "tags"]
#>      tags
#>    <list>
#> 1:       
#> 2:     io
